Hannah —

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Legal reached out with two follow ups before we route Appendix B for signature:

1) We need a written description of the purge gating logic — Medivent requires that backups are not purged until: (a) the DPA Appendix B is fully executed, and (b) Redwood has provided a signed attestation listing all subprocessors involved in backup storage/restore and log processing.

2) Because we operate across US/EU boundaries, we need confirmation you will not run any crossborder purge job for EU-scoped customer data until the Data Transfer Agreement (DTA) is in place.

Can you send a short operational note that our Security team can attach to their sign-off? Ideally: one page that describes staggered erase windows (ephemeral logs vs backups), the gating checks we run, and the fallback/rollback path if a purge is triggered in error.

Also, please list the estimated time between DPA signing and first eligible purge for non-EU data and the retention carveouts (for forensic/legal holds).

Regards,

Carlos —

Appreciate the clear asks. I prepared a concise operational note below and attached a draft runbook for your ops/security reviewers. High-level answers first:

- Purge gating: Redwood will gate backup deletions behind two checks — (1) executed DPA Appendix B & DTA where applicable, and (2) completed subprocessor attestations covering backup storage, snapshot orchestration, and log-indexing services. No automatic purge job will remove backups if either check is unmet.
- EU data: Absolutely — we will not schedule any crossborder purge for EU-scoped datasets until the DTA is executed and the transfer mechanism is approved.
- Typical timeline: once Appendix B + attestations are executed, non-EU eligible backups will queue for purge after a 30-day cooling period to allow for late holds/appeals; actual purge execution target is 60 days post-signing in standard cases. EU timeline is gated and will not start until DTA is in place.

Please see the operational note pasted below and the attached runbook (redwood-purge-runbook-v1.md) with checklist items for your SOC team. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want line-by-line.

Operational note (one page):

1) Scope and definitions
- Backup snapshots: immutable weekly snapshots stored in object-store tier (snap-YYYYMMDD).
- Ephemeral logs (KV logs): short-term runtime logs used for inference routing and debugging; typically TTL 7–14 days unless customer requests extended retention.
- Purge gating: the logical AND of executable legal instruments (DPA Appendix B + DTA where required) and complete subprocessor attestations for systems that can restore or rehydrate data.

2) Staggered erase windows
- Phase 1 (ephemeral): KV logs and ephemeral caches are eligible for automated eviction per configured TTL; these are not considered backups and purging them does not require DPA Appendix B execution.
- Phase 2 (snapshots): Immutable backups are eligible only after purge gating is satisfied. Once gating is satisfied, snapshots enter a 30-day cooling period before being marked for deletion. Final purge occurs during a scheduled maintenance window and is irreversible.

3) Subprocessor attestations
- Redwood will provide a signed attestation that lists subprocessors involved in: snapshot storage, snapshot orchestration, cross-region replication, and log indexing. The attestation includes the subprocessor name, logical role, and last security attestation date.

4) Rollback & safety controls
- Safe-delete flag: before destructive operations, snapshots are moved to a quarantine state for 48 hours and a safe-delete flag is set. On detection of legal hold or proactive appeal, quarantine is reverted and deletion is canceled.
- Immutable snapshot checkpoints: we maintain an immutable chain-id for each snapshot; rollback requires an authorized ops ticket plus CISO approval.

5) Exceptions & forensic holds
- Legal holds: any certified legal hold submitted by Medivent contact will automatically block purge jobs for associated customer IDs until hold removal.
- Emergency forensic hold: 24/7 on-call will accept signed eDiscovery requests; we will isolate and copy relevant snapshots to an escrow bucket (access-logged) pending coordination.

6) Timeline summary
- Post-signature (non-EU): 30-day cooling -> 60-day target purge window (unless hold).
- EU data: purge not scheduled until DTA executed and crossborder transfer mechanism approved.

Next steps: Kimberly/Laura will produce the formal attestation and the subprocessor CSV. I will share the runbook with your team.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
